add.issue.name: llama-swap stats poller reloads a model right after it is unloaded

edit.description.md:
LlamaSwapStats polls `GET <host>/upstream/<model>/slots` once a second. llama-swap treats a request on its /upstream proxy as demand and loads the model, so a manual unload is undone within about a second: `/running` shows the model `starting` again right after `POST /api/models/unload`. TTL unloads stick only because the model leaves `/running` before the next poll.

Fix: poll only while the model's state is `ready`, and when llama-swap is on loopback, read `/slots` straight from the backend port listed in `/running` (`proxy`). A stopped backend refuses the connection instead of loading anything. Remote hosts keep the /upstream path, gated on `ready`.

Verify: unload the loaded model with the shell running; `/running` stays empty, and the stats still update during generation.

add.issue.comment.md: Solution: PR #262 (fix/llama-swap-stats-no-reload). Verified live with the patched file in the installed shell: after `POST /api/models/unload`, `/running` stayed empty for 20 s (before the fix it was `starting` again within half a second). A generation afterwards worked, no new /upstream slot polls appeared, and the widget had open connections to the backend port. How the stats look on screen is for review.

add.issue.name: Settings: choose render GPU (iGPU-only / dGPU) and persist across install.sh

edit.description.md:
## Problem
On a hybrid box (Intel iGPU `00:02.0` + Nvidia RTX `01:00.0`), Hyprland picks the Nvidia card as its primary renderer if a monitor is on it at login, and keeps it after unplugging. Hyprland, Xwayland, kitty, qs and Discord then hold about 840 MiB of VRAM. The operator needs the RTX card at 0 MiB for llama-swap (global rule: the GPU belongs to llama-swap only).

Today this is fixed by hand in `~/.config/hypr/custom.lua`, which `install.sh` and `aphotic update` don't overwrite:
```lua
hl.env("AQ_DRM_DEVICES", "/dev/dri/card1")
hl.env("__EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES", "/usr/share/glvnd/egl_vendor.d/50_mesa.json")
hl.env("__GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME", "mesa")
hl.env("LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME", "iHD")
```
`hyprland.conf` is overwritten on install, and `install.sh` appends `require("nvidia")`, which sets `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia`.

## Ask
Add a Settings.qml option, "Render GPU", with these choices:
- **iGPU only**: Hyprland and all clients render on the iGPU; dGPU-attached ports go dark.
- **dGPU / hybrid**: current behaviour, Nvidia ports work.
- (optional) **Auto**: whatever Hyprland picks.

## Requirements
- Persist the choice in a generated file that install and update never overwrite, e.g. `~/.config/hypr/gpu.lua` required after `nvidia.lua`, or the existing user-state store. It must survive `install.sh` and `aphotic update`.
- Resolve the card **by PCI path** (`/dev/dri/by-path/pci-*-card`), not `cardN`. The numbering can change between boots. Note that `AQ_DRM_DEVICES` is colon-separated, so a by-path link can't be passed directly. Resolve it to `/dev/dri/cardN` at session start, or add a udev symlink without a colon.
- In iGPU mode, also override the EGL/GLX vendor and VA-API driver (above), so clients don't open `/dev/nvidia0`.
- Show in the UI that the change applies at the next login, and offer a "log out now" button.
- Detect the GPUs from `/dev/dri/by-path` and hide the option on single-GPU systems.

## Done when
- In iGPU mode after relogin, `nvidia-smi` lists no processes and shows about 0 MiB used.
- Re-running `install.sh` keeps the setting.
- Switching back to dGPU and relogging restores the Nvidia-connected output (DP-2).
- Then remove the manual block from the operator's `custom.lua`.

Ref: Qt/Quickshell API docs in `~/docs-local`.

add.issue.name: Fresh install renders icon names as text: Material Symbols missing from font cache

edit.description.md:
On a fresh install the bar, popouts and panes show glyph names ("wifi", "volume_up") instead of icons. `ttf-material-symbols-variable` is installed, but `fc-list | grep -c "Material Symbols"` returns 0 until the user runs `fc-cache -f` and restarts the shell.

Cause: install.sh installs packages one pacman transaction at a time, so the fontconfig hook runs every second or two while fonts keep landing in `/usr/share/fonts/TTF`. Fontconfig trusts a directory cache whose stored mtime matches the directory's, at one-second resolution, so a font added in the same second as the previous cache write can drop out of the cache.

Fix:
- Force a font cache rebuild once after the package lists finish, before the shell starts.
- Check that fontconfig resolves Material Symbols Rounded and warn with the fix if it does not.
- `aphotic doctor` reports the same check so affected installs can find and repair it.

add.issue.comment.md: PR #289 into dev. Reproduced the race on fontconfig 2.18.3: a font copied in within the same second as the previous cache write and followed by a plain `fc-cache` was missing in 9 of 10 runs, and `fc-cache -f` fixed it every time. The fix rebuilds both caches once after the main package list, checks the icon font, and adds an "Icon font" check to `aphotic doctor`.

add.issue.name: NVIDIA config lost on sync, and hybrid laptops get desktop-only NVIDIA settings

edit.description.md:
Reported on a Dell laptop with an Intel i7 11th gen iGPU and an NVIDIA T500 (Turing, 2 GB): the NVIDIA session settings did not seem applied.

Findings:
- `aphotic sync` / `aphotic update` run `install.sh --config-only`, which recopies `hyprland.lua` but skips NVIDIA detection, so `ISNVIDIA` is empty and the appended `require("nvidia")` is dropped. Every NVIDIA machine loses its settings after the first sync.
- Nothing detects hybrid graphics. `nvidia.lua` forces `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia` on Optimus laptops where the iGPU drives the panel, and `libva-nvidia-driver` is never installed, so VA-API breaks.
- mkinitcpio loads the NVIDIA modules without `i915` first, which Hyprland's docs call out for hybrid Intel laptops (Electron/Chromium stalls after boot).
- No `prime-run`, so there is no supported way to send an app to the dGPU.

Fix:
- Detect NVIDIA (and hybrid) in the config-only path too.
- Detect an Intel/AMD iGPU next to the NVIDIA card. On hybrid, skip `require("nvidia")`, load the iGPU's kernel driver before the NVIDIA modules, and install `nvidia-prime`.
- Install `libva-nvidia-driver` on NVIDIA-only machines, where `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia` stays.

Out of scope: pinning the render GPU with `AQ_DRM_DEVICES`, which belongs to 026WW1M.

add.issue.comment.md: PR #290 into dev. Fork from the original plan: hybrid is detected from connected DRM outputs, not from lspci alone. The lspci rule called any machine with both GPUs hybrid, including a desktop with the iGPU enabled and monitors on the NVIDIA card, which would have lost its NVIDIA settings. Now hybrid means a non-NVIDIA GPU drives a connected display while an NVIDIA card is present. Implementation drafted by pi/coder, reviewed and corrected by claude.

add.issue.name: CI: a local runner and log triage that agents can use

edit.description.md:
Tests that pass in a working checkout can fail in CI. The CI checkout is shallow and detached, with no `origin/main` and no gitignored files. Agents can't reproduce those failures locally, and the raw `--log-failed` output buries the one useful line under thousands of runner lines.

- `tools/ci/local.sh`: runs the required checks in a CI-shaped checkout and prints only the failing blocks.
- `tools/ci/triage.py <pr>`: splits required checks from advisory ones and prints the failing test blocks from a red run.
- AGENTS.md: a short CI section with both commands and a list of what the CI environment lacks.

add.issue.name: Flow v2 model: workloads occupy resource regions instead of linking to them

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** Flow draws resources on the left, workloads on the right, and one curve per claim between them. With two engines, a game and a build, the curves cross into a tangle, and draw cost grows with resources x workloads.

**Plan.** Change `FlowModel.build` to output regions, not edges. Each region holds the workloads that occupy it:
- one GPU region per card (`gpu-vram/<deviceId>`): VRAM segments per claimant, measured and claimed, headroom
- memory: PSS segments per workload, host cache kept separate
- CPU: per-thread load, with each workload's share
- storage: read and write rate per workload, no capacity
- bus: an engine whose report splits placement across GPU and RAM gets one entry linking both segments

Every workload gets a stable identity (hue index, glyph) that the scene reuses in every region. Keep `workFor`, `receiptsFor` and `projection` as they are.

**Depends on** K95NG1X for per-workload CPU, PSS and disk data.

**Done when.** Unit tests cover a 96 GB two-engine host, a 16 GB card with an expert-offload engine, a GPU-less CPU host, and a game plus a build. Output size scales with the number of regions, not with claims.

add.issue.name: Flow v2 scene: a cross-section of the machine

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** Flow's map panel cannot show RAM, CPU, per-card VRAM and disk for many workloads at once without turning into a mess of lines. It should feel like looking inside the machine.

**Plan.** Replace the map panel in `FlowScene.qml` with a topology view fed by the Flow v2 model:
- a die per GPU card, drawn as a ring of VRAM arcs per claimant. A negotiation turns the contested arc to the warning colour
- a memory bank band, a CPU lattice with one cell per thread, a storage lane along the bottom
- one bus between GPU and memory. An engine that splits a model across both shows one shape spanning the bus
- selecting a workload draws a single trace through its footprints and dims the rest. No always-on lines
- the side rail keeps the roster, work, receipts and negotiation controls

Darkness at rest, light where compute is live, using the light language from FA067FQ. Original design in native QML (`Shape`, one optional `ShaderEffect`). No web engine, no copied assets.

**Depends on** the Flow v2 model ticket.

**Done when.** The operator signs off on the visuals on a live desktop, and the fidelity dial ticket's cost targets hold.

add.issue.name: Flow fidelity dial: off, minimal, abstract, full

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** Some users want Flow as rich as their render GPU allows. Others need it to cost almost nothing. Today there is one Motion toggle.

**Plan.** Add `Settings.flowFidelity`, which replaces the Motion toggle:
- `off`: text summary only, updated when the data changes
- `minimal`: static `Shape` geometry with flat fills, rebuilt only on a data tick, no animation
- `abstract`: adds glow pulses and bus flow on one 12 Hz timer
- `full`: adds one shader pass and particles on the bus and storage lane, at display rate

Everything stays inside Flow's visibility-gated loader, so closed Flow costs nothing. No per-frame Canvas repaint. Gaming shelter and battery drop one tier and restore it on release.

**Done when.** With Flow open, `minimal` adds single-digit MB of RSS and under 1% CPU, and `abstract` stays near the 12 Hz screensaver budget. No tier opens a GPU compute context (`nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps` shows nothing new). Numbers are measured and recorded per tier.

add.issue.name: Spike: detect which GPU composites the desktop

edit.description.md:
**Question.** Can the shell tell whether Hyprland renders on an integrated GPU or on the card that runs inference? The Flow fidelity dial should default to `abstract` when the desktop renders on a different GPU from the one under load, and to `minimal` when they share a card.

**Try.** Which `/dev/dri/card*` or render node the Hyprland PID holds open, `AQ_DRM_DEVICES`, and `hyprctl` output. Map the result to the same `deviceId` the VRAM resources use (PCI bus ID).

**Done when.** A short write-up in a comment names a method that works on a hybrid laptop, an iGPU plus dGPU desktop, and a single-GPU box, or says it cannot be done reliably.

add.issue.name: Engine descriptors ship as a plugin [engine] capability

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** Engine descriptors (id, label, host setting key, key-store key, process match, endpoint, capabilities) would still live in core. Every new engine, including one a user builds themselves, would need a core PR, and engine ids would sit in core files.

**Plan.** Add an `[engine]` manifest block that the plugin registry reads, the same way `[cli]` works. Fields: the descriptor above plus `protocol`, either a built-in parser name or the versioned engine report from the inference desktop plan. The generic engine adapter consumes descriptors from both core and plugins. Core keeps descriptors only for what the `ai` layer installs or already supports (Ollama, llama.cpp, llama-swap, LM Studio). Strata and NInfer move to the plugin repository as the first two engine plugins.

**Done when.** A plugin with only a `plugin.toml` and a mock server shows a model, PID and claims in Flow with no core edit. Installing and removing it adds and removes the engine. No core file names Strata or NInfer.

add.issue.name: Install: bring your own engine, ai layer without Ollama

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** The `ai` layer installs Ollama. New users want that. Users who already run llama.cpp, a custom CUDA engine or anything else get a second engine they never asked for.

**Plan.** Add an installer choice (and a matching flag) for the `ai` layer: Ollama as today, or bring your own engine. The second path skips Ollama and its acceleration package and keeps every other part of the layer. Chat providers and Flow then find the user's engine through the existing adapters or an engine plugin.

**Done when.** A disposable VM install with the option set has no Ollama package or service, the AI pane offers to attach an engine, and an update does not add Ollama back.

add.issue.name: aphotic engine new: scaffold for a home-built engine

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** Someone writing their own CUDA or C++ engine should be able to light it up in Aphotic in an afternoon.

**Plan.** A `cli` plugin command, `aphotic engine new <name>`, that writes an engine plugin skeleton: `plugin.toml` with an `[engine]` block, plus a single-header C++ reference that serves the engine report over loopback, including the GPU and RAM placement split. Point at the model library and fit tooling for split suggestions on the user's card.

**Depends on** the `[engine]` capability ticket and a published engine report version.

**Done when.** The scaffold builds, its sample server appears in Flow, and the plugin guide documents it.

add.issue.name: Signal is the design language; the bar style is only a layout

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** Signal is one bar skin under the full style. About 74 files switch their look on `Settings.barSignal`, so dock, taskbar, minimal and capsule (the fresh-install default) turn the Signal look off across the whole shell. Users have to hunt for it, and the other bar styles feel out of place.

**Plan.**
- Settings: `barSkin` splits into `barLayout` (full, capsule, dock, taskbar, minimal), a per-layout signal skin id (default `signal`) and `corners` (sharp, soft, round). Migration: signal to full/sharp, square to full/soft, pill to full/round. `barSignal` and every Signal branch go away. Signal is always on.
- New `components/SignalLine.qml`, extracted from the full bar's existing line (hairline halves, a gap for the notch, a hover segment, an accent under the active workspace), with idle, active and warn states. 12 Hz max, static when motion is off.
- New `components/SignalSurface.qml` (glass, hairline, edge light).
- Each layout gets its own Signal skin built from these: full on the inner edge, capsule along its lower edge, dock under the dock with lit segments under apps, taskbar along the top edge with the focused task lit, minimal where the line is the bar.
- Settings > Bar shows layouts that already wear Signal, plus a corner choice. The separate Signal card goes.
- IPC `bar.setSkin` and `aphotic bar style` keep working.

**Done when.** All five layouts show Signal on a live desktop, every old setting migrates, the probe instantiates each layout, and idle cost per layout does not rise.

add.issue.name: Signal spec and one reference surface

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** Every surface invents its own spacing, radius, hover and colour. Without one written reference, a refresh drifts back into that.

**Plan.** A one-page Signal spec covering line states and tones, spacing scale, type scale, corners, interaction (hover, press, focus), icon weight and motion budget. Show it on one reference surface, the full bar plus one popout, and have the operator sign it off on a live desktop. Every later surface copies it.

**Done when.** The spec is in the repo and the operator has approved the reference surface.

add.issue.name: Design ratchet: a test that counts Material leftovers and only lets the number fall

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** "Remove the Material feel" has no measure, so it never finishes.

**Plan.** `tests/test_design_language.py` counts: raw hex colours, numeric radii, `m3*` palette reads outside `Colours.qml`, `StateLayer` and `MaterialIcon` uses, Signal on/off branches, and comments naming other projects. It stores a baseline and fails CI when any count rises. Starting point: 1297 `m3*` reads across 168 files, 83 `StateLayer`, 100 `MaterialIcon`, about 74 Signal-branching files.

**Done when.** The test runs in CI, the baseline is committed, and every 2.1.0 PR reports its delta. The counts reach zero before the release PR.

add.issue.name: Aphotic tokens: spacing, type and corners without the Material scale

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** `config/Tokens.qml` copies a Material 3 scale (extraSmall to largeIncreased, `rounding.full: 999999`, headline/body/label/title type roles), and call sites pick sizes inline.

**Plan.** An Aphotic scale: numbered spacing steps, one type scale, and radius tokens that resolve through the `corners` setting, so pill and square shapes live on as a preference on every surface. Replace Material shadow levels (`Elevation.qml`) with edge light and hairline depth, keeping shadows only where a surface floats over app content. Old names stay as aliases until the sweep is done, then go.

**Done when.** No file reads the old names, and switching corners reshapes every surface consistently.

add.issue.name: Semantic colour roles; m3 names stay inside Colours

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** QML reads raw `m3*` palette roles 1297 times across 168 files, so every surface makes its own colour decisions.

**Plan.** Add roles to `Colours`: ink, inkMuted, surface, raised, glass, hairline, edgeLight, signal, warn, alert. Derive them from the generated palette and the existing Signal tones. `m3*` stays internal to `Colours.qml`, because the palette generator emits it.

**Done when.** No QML outside `Colours.qml` reads `m3*`, and every theme still renders with correct contrast.

add.issue.name: Interact replaces the ripple

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** `components/StateLayer.qml` is the Material ripple and hover layer, used in 83 files. It is the most recognisable Material tell after the icons.

**Plan.** `components/Interact.qml` with the same API surface: hover lights the edge and brightens the line, press is a brief inset, keyboard focus shows the signal line. No circular ripple, no shape morph. Migrate call sites mechanically.

**Done when.** `StateLayer` has no users, and hover, press and focus feel the same on every surface.

add.issue.name: Thin-stroke icon set replaces Material Symbols

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** Material Symbols Rounded, drawn through `MaterialIcon.qml` in 100 files, makes the shell read as Material at a glance.

**Plan.** Choose an MIT- or ISC-licensed line icon set whose stroke matches the hairline weight, by measuring how many of the glyph names we actually use it covers. Rename `MaterialIcon.qml` to `Icon.qml` (the old name stays as a shim) and add a name map so call sites keep working. Add the package to both base profiles. Keep the "glyph" kind in custom app icons working.

**Done when.** No Material Symbols glyph renders anywhere, the font is out of both profiles, and custom app icons still resolve.

add.issue.name: Aphotic, not Aphotic-Hypr: product name, repo and install path

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** The product is Aphotic. Hyprland is the compositor underneath, but the name says otherwise.

**Plan.**
- Use Aphotic everywhere a user sees it: About, README, site, wiki, installer banner and SPDX lines.
- User-facing text says "compositor" except where the user has to act on Hyprland config.
- Rename the GitHub repo to `aphotic`; GitHub redirects the old URLs.
- The clone directory becomes `~/Aphotic`. `APHOTIC_DOTS_DIR` falls back to `~/Aphotic-Hypr`, and `aphotic update` offers a one-time move with a compatibility symlink.
- History is never rewritten.

**Done when.** A fresh VM install lands in `~/Aphotic`, an existing `~/Aphotic-Hypr` install updates cleanly, and no user-visible string says Aphotic-Hypr.

add.issue.name: Custom bar skins: users and plugins swap the Signal style

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** Once each layout has a Signal skin behind one contract, users will want to write their own.

**Plan.** Open the bar skin contract (layout, chrome, line, geometry) to `~/.config/aphotic/bar-skins/<name>/` and to plugins through a `[ui.bar_skin]` manifest block. Settings lists installed skins per layout. A broken skin falls back to the built-in Signal skin with a notice.

**Depends on** the Signal language ticket. Not required for 2.1.0.

add.issue.name: Release 2.1.0

edit.description.md:
**Plan.** Once the Signal language, foundations, surface sweep, rename and Flow v2 have landed on dev: open the dev to main PR, tag v2.1.0, write the release notes and refresh the site gallery.

**Done when.** The design ratchet reads zero, all required checks pass on the release PR, and the operator has signed off every surface on a live desktop.

add.issue.name: Refine: bar widgets and popouts

edit.description.md:
Bring every bar widget and popout (network, bluetooth, audio, battery, media, resources, agents, task groups, settings, window, keyboard) onto the Signal spec.

Checklist (shared by every refine ticket): tokens only; semantic colour roles only; Interact instead of StateLayer; Icon instead of MaterialIcon; signal line where state lives; copy pass (plain, no jargon, no engine names); comment pass (only non-obvious workarounds and safety notes; no other projects named). Nothing removed. Design ratchet count falls.

Depends on the Signal language, tokens, colour roles, Interact and icon tickets.

add.issue.name: Refine: notch and its tiles

edit.description.md:
Bring the notch, its tabs and every core tile onto the Signal spec. The notch gap in the bar's signal line and the notch's own edge should read as one continuous line.

Checklist: same as the bar refine ticket (tokens, roles, Interact, Icon, signal line, copy pass, comment pass, nothing removed, ratchet falls).

add.issue.name: Refine: launcher and command palette

edit.description.md:
Bring the launcher (list and grid), the command palette and package search onto the Signal spec. The selected row is marked by the signal line, not a filled pill.

Checklist: same as the bar refine ticket.

add.issue.name: Refine: notifications, notification center and OSD

edit.description.md:
Bring toasts, the notification center and history, and the OSD sliders onto the Signal spec. Urgency maps onto line states: normal is idle, critical is warn.

Checklist: same as the bar refine ticket.

add.issue.name: Refine: dashboard and its tabs

edit.description.md:
Bring the dashboard shell, quick toggles, media, workspaces tab and AI chat tab onto the Signal spec. The AI chat tab carries the most Signal branches in the codebase (42) and is the largest single cleanup.

Checklist: same as the bar refine ticket. AI copy names no engine.

add.issue.name: Refine: settings panel, rail and panes

edit.description.md:
Bring the settings panel, category rail, shared rows and sections, and every pane onto the Signal spec. The shared settings components carry the pattern, so most panes follow from fixing those.

Checklist: same as the bar refine ticket. Long help text gets a stop-slop pass.

add.issue.name: Refine: lock screen, greeter and session menu

edit.description.md:
Bring the lock screen, the greeter and the session menu onto the Signal spec. The shader text reveal (`SignalText`), unused today, gives the lock clock and wordmark their moment.

Checklist: same as the bar refine ticket.

add.issue.name: Refine: switcher, workspace view and wallpaper picker

edit.description.md:
Bring the window switcher, the workspace plane and the wallpaper picker and dock onto the Signal spec.

Checklist: same as the bar refine ticket.

add.issue.name: Refine: keybind cheatsheet and intelligence window

edit.description.md:
Bring the keybind cheatsheet (25 Signal branches) and the intelligence window onto the Signal spec.

Checklist: same as the bar refine ticket.

add.issue.name: Refine: first-party plugin surfaces

edit.description.md:
Bring the first-party plugins' surfaces (agent graph and tiles, dev ports, gaming, llama-swap, pet, visualizer, screensaver, live wallpaper) onto the Signal spec, through the same shared components core uses, so a plugin never looks bolted on.

Checklist: same as the bar refine ticket. Lands in the plugin repository.

Note: local feature/strata-backend is 5 commits ahead and 1 behind origin (a rebase that was never pushed), so the PR on GitHub still shows the older version. add.issue.comment.md:
Live evidence, 2026-10-06: an engine served through llama-swap (ready on 127.0.0.1:5803, 23 GB VRAM per nvidia-smi) does not appear in Flow at all. llama-swap's /running lists it and the host is configured, but `LlamaSwapClaims.qml` resolves PIDs with `pgrep -x llama-server`, so any process not named llama-server never gets a PID or a VRAM claim.

Operator requirement: nothing in core may depend on one engine's name or project. Two layers fix this for every engine:
1. Driver first. Every PID the GPU driver lists as holding VRAM (nvidia-smi compute apps today, AMD/Intel equivalents later) becomes a claimant, adapter or not. An unknown engine shows as its process name and real VRAM.
2. PID by port, not by name. Routers report a proxy URL (llama-swap `proxy: http://localhost:5803`); resolve the PID that listens on that port. The same works for any engine behind any router.

RAM, CPU and disk read come from the PID observer in this ticket; `/proc/<pid>/io` read_bytes covers engines that stream weights from SSD. Adapters only enrich (model name, GPU/RAM split) and are never required for visibility. Prove it with the engine above, Ollama, LM Studio, a llama.cpp server and an unknown binary holding VRAM.
add.issue.comment.author: 82D6ZVRHW7Q89JK5Z846NWXBMY

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** Harness names are hardcoded in core: the bar metadata table in `AgentProviders.qml` (claude, codex, opencode), the role list in `AgentRoles.qml`, and the transcript scan in `agent_usage.py` (claude and codex). The `harness` data gate (`hasConfiguredHarness`) only passes when Claude or Codex is logged in, so a user with only OpenCode, Pi or a custom harness never gets the agent tile, graph or audit. Any record without a harness name defaults to `claude`.

**Plan.**
- A harness descriptor: id, label, icon, process match, launch command, where its events land, how to read its usage and context. Sources: a `[harness]` plugin manifest block (each hook plugin ships its own) and user drop-ins in `~/.config/aphotic/harnesses/<name>.toml`, so a user or their agent can add a harness without a core change.
- `AgentProviders`, `AgentRoles` and `agent_usage.py` read descriptors instead of their tables. No core file names a harness.
- The `harness` gate passes when any descriptor is installed.
- Records with no harness name read as `unknown`, never `claude`.
- Settings lets users choose which harnesses show, their order and the default, keeping launch and cycle behaviour.

**Done when.** Claude, Codex, OpenCode and one drop-in custom harness all appear with no harness name in core, and an OpenCode-only machine gets the agent surfaces.

**Problem.** The AI notch tile belongs to one router's plugin and reads only that router's models. Other engines are invisible there, and only Ollama can be started or stopped anywhere. Nothing can load a model or switch one.

**Plan.** The tile reads the shared local inference registry, so every engine shows: the router, direct servers and any engine a plugin or drop-in descriptor adds. Per engine it shows state, model, VRAM and RAM. It offers the controls that engine's descriptor declares (start, stop, load, unload, switch model) through action receipts, settled when the engine confirms. Model choice is a dropdown with a real draggable scrollbar, not wheel-only. Routers and direct engines stay distinct, and a model behind a router keeps one physical owner.

**Depends on** the engine control capabilities (A9Q1R0G) for anything past unload.

**Done when.** Every running engine on the machine appears, unload works for each engine that supports it, and start, stop, load and switch work for each engine whose descriptor declares them, each with a receipt.

add.issue.comment.md: Scope addition (operator, 2026-10-06). Descriptors also load from user drop-ins in `~/.config/aphotic/engines/<name>.toml`, not only plugins, so a user's agent can register an engine it just installed. Descriptors declare control capabilities, each optional: `start`/`stop` (Aphotic runs the command as a transient user service it tracks; it never kills a process it did not start), `load`/`unload`/`switch` (HTTP call or command), and `models` (how to list what can be loaded). Every control goes through action receipts and settles on the engine's own report, never on the HTTP status alone. Today only Ollama has start/stop and nothing can load or switch.
add.issue.comment.author: 82D6ZVRHW7Q89JK5Z846NWXBMY

add.issue.name: Agent tile and graph: every harness, honest idle states

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** The agent tile and graph show one latest session and treat unnamed records as Claude, so other harnesses never appear. States are wrong: `compacting` reads as "no session", a session that ends without a session_end record stays idle forever, and the bar popout picks running or idle from the last event name instead of the tracked session status.

**Plan.** States per harness, from its descriptor and its events:
- **none**: no harness installed or open. The tile shows a quiet idle face, and the gate still offers it when any harness is installed.
- **open, idle**: the harness process runs (descriptor process match) but no turn is live.
- **active**: a turn or tool call is running.
- **waiting**: the harness waits on the user. The click focuses its window, as today.
- **compacting**: shown as its own state.
- **ended**: also set when the harness process exits without a session_end.

The tile lists every live harness, not one. The graph draws every harness's sessions, subagents and models, plus engine nodes from the shared inference registry instead of one router. Replay works for any harness's archived runs.

**Depends on** J3KTGS1 (descriptors).

**Done when.** Claude, Codex, OpenCode and a custom harness running at once each show the right state in the tile, the graph and replay, and every state above can be reached on a live desktop.

add.issue.name: Usage, cost and context for every harness

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** Only Claude Code gets tile stats: 5h, 7d and context bars come from its statusline, and today's tokens come from a transcript scan of two harnesses. The v2 contract already carries usage (input, output, reasoning, cache), cost and quota for any harness, and OpenCode already sends cost on every turn, yet no reader shows it.

**Plan.** The tile and graph read v2 `usage` and `quota` records for any harness:
- per-session and today's tokens and cost
- context fill when the harness reports it
- quota windows when the harness has them

The quota file gains one entry per harness instead of only Claude's. Harness descriptors say where a harness's stats come from (events, a statusline, a transcript), so `agent_usage.py` scans what the descriptors name. A missing number shows as absent, never as zero or a guess.

**Done when.** OpenCode shows cost and context from its own records, Codex shows tokens, and a custom harness that emits usage shows the same stats as Claude Code.

add.issue.name: aphotic agent emit and agent run: any harness can report

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** A harness without a hook system, or a home-built agent loop, has no way into the agent stream short of writing JSON lines by hand.

**Plan.** Two commands:
- `aphotic agent emit <event> [--session ID] [--harness NAME] [--model M] [--tokens-in N ...]` writes one validated v2 record through the existing writer.
- `aphotic agent run --harness NAME -- <command>` wraps any command: it emits session_start and session_end around it, and marks the session active while the process runs and uses CPU.

Both work for Pi, Oh-My-Pi, dsh, Empryo or any custom harness until each gets a native adapter (FJXMJ10, ZG4V11V).

**Done when.** A shell-script agent that calls `aphotic agent emit` appears in the tile and graph with its usage, and a wrapped command shows open, active and ended on its own.

add.issue.name: AI tab engine panel: start, stop, load, unload and switch

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** The dashboard AI tab and the AI settings pane control only Ollama (host, start and stop, model picker, pull). Every other engine has a host field at most.

**Plan.** One engine panel, shared by the AI tab and the settings pane and fed by the same registry as the AI notch tile. One row per engine: state, model, VRAM, RAM, and the controls its descriptor declares:
- start and stop
- a scrollable model dropdown (with a draggable scrollbar) to load or switch
- unload

A router lists its models and switches between them. Ollama's existing controls move onto the same row shape. Every action shows its receipt inline.

**Depends on** A9Q1R0G (control capabilities) and G18Z0ZA (shared registry in the tile).

**Done when.** On this machine the panel starts and stops a direct server, switches a router's model, loads and unloads an Ollama model, and shows an engine added by a drop-in descriptor, all without engine names in core.

add.issue.name: Agent kit: a guide that lets the user's own agent set up engines and harnesses

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** AI users already have an agent that installs and configures things for them. Aphotic gives that agent nothing to work with, so every new engine or harness means a change to Aphotic.

**Plan.** With the AI layer enabled, `aphotic ai guide` writes `~/.config/aphotic/AGENTS.aphotic.md` and the same content as a skill for harnesses that load skills. It documents the stable surfaces an agent may use:
- engine descriptor drop-ins (`~/.config/aphotic/engines/`) with their control commands
- harness descriptor drop-ins (`~/.config/aphotic/harnesses/`)
- `aphotic agent emit` and `aphotic agent run`
- `--json` output on the status, engine, model and harness commands
- which actions an agent may take alone and which need the user's confirmation. Start, stop, load and unload go through action receipts. Nothing destructive runs automatically.

Aphotic never edits the user's own `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`: the command prints the include line, and adds it only with `--link`. The guide regenerates on update so it matches the installed version. Gated on the AI layer; absent when AI is off or blocked (RQW9JE4).

**Done when.** On a fresh AI install, a coding agent given only the guide installs a new engine, registers it with one descriptor file, and the AI tile and Flow show it with working controls, with no Aphotic code change.

add.issue.comment.md: Current state (code map 2026-10-06): codex-hooks wires `~/.codex/hooks.json` and `codex_hook.py` sends v1-shaped payloads with `harness="codex"` through agent_hook.py. No provider, no usage, no quota, so the agent tile can show a Codex session but no stats. For this ticket: emit native v2 (session_start, turn, tool_call, usage with tokens, session_end), set the provider, and ship a `[harness]` descriptor (J3KTGS1) so Codex shows in the agent tile, graph and replay with its own stats (W4BEZ7Q).
add.issue.comment.author: 82D6ZVRHW7Q89JK5Z846NWXBMY

add.issue.name: AGENTS.md: never overwrite an existing CLAUDE.md, structure over features

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** AGENTS.md tells agents to `cp AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md` when their tool reads a different file. On a machine that already has its own CLAUDE.md (a maintainer's or a contributor's), an agent following that line literally destroys it. AGENTS.md also never says how to add a capability, so agents add one-off code paths.

**Plan.** Change the copy line to: copy only when the target does not exist, never overwrite it. Add a short "Structure over features" section: extend through plugins, descriptors, drop-in config and the `aphotic` CLI; no engine, harness, model or project names in core; no second way to do one thing; propose the extension point before building. Keep it to a few lines.

**Done when.** Merged into dev.

add.issue.name: Developer SDK: one entry point for contributors

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** A new contributor has the plugin guide, the wiki and CONTRIBUTING.md, but no single page that says how to set up to work on Aphotic itself: which channel to daily drive, where to test, how to build and verify.

**Plan.** A `Developer-SDK` wiki page as the hub, and a Develop page on the site that links to it. Sections, each linking out rather than repeating:
- daily drive and test channels
- dev VM (Proxmox, other hypervisors)
- build and verify (tests, `tools/ci/local.sh`, headless QML probe)
- writing plugins
- engine and harness descriptors
- the agent kit
- shipping a PR

Add one line to AGENTS.md pointing an agent at the page when the user has a hypervisor or dev environment. Stop-slop every page. No gitignored paths, no lab-specific values.

**Done when.** A new contributor can go from the hub to a running dev VM and a passing local CI run without asking. The AGENTS.md line is merged.

add.issue.name: Dev VM on Proxmox: a tracked, parameterised script

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** The maintainer runs Aphotic as a disposable Proxmox dev VM: Arch cloud image, template, clone, reset in minutes. The script lives outside the repo with one lab's host, IDs, addresses and user hardcoded, so no contributor can use it.

**Plan.** `tools/devvm/proxmox.sh` with `template`, `reset`, `destroy`, `status` and `install --channel edge|<branch>`.
- Every site value (PVE host, storage, bridge, VM and template IDs, static IP or DHCP, user, SSH key) comes from `~/.config/aphotic/devvm.env`. `proxmox.sh init` writes a commented example.
- No default points at anyone's network.
- The VM uses `virtio-gl` so a real Hyprland session runs.
- `install` runs the installer inside the VM over SSH.

**Done when.** On a stock Proxmox host, `init`, `template`, `reset` and `install --channel edge` produce a VM that logs into an Aphotic session. Shellcheck passes, and a test covers argument parsing and config loading without a hypervisor.

add.issue.name: Dev VM anywhere else: requirements and an agent-adaptable guide

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** Contributors without Proxmox need a dev VM too, and their own agent can build one if it knows the requirements.

**Plan.** A `Dev-VM` wiki page:
- **Requirements, stated so an agent can satisfy them on any hypervisor:** Arch x86_64 cloud image or ISO, a GPU path Hyprland accepts (virtio-gl or virgl, or GPU passthrough), RAM and disk minimums, SSH key access, cloud-init or a first-boot script.
- **Free first:** a worked example for libvirt/QEMU on the contributor's own machine.
- **Proxmox:** links the Proxmox script.
- **Advanced, for people who already rent one:** a VPS section that states the limit plainly. A VPS with no GPU or virtual display cannot run a Hyprland session, so it only suits headless install and CLI tests.
- **A short prompt block** a contributor can hand their agent to adapt the requirements to their environment.

**Done when.** The libvirt example produces a VM that logs into Aphotic, and the page passes stop-slop.

add.issue.name: Contributor workflow: daily drive stable, test edge and PR branches in a VM

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** `install.sh --channel stable|edge` exists, but nothing tells a contributor how to combine channels: a working desktop on stable and a VM for dev builds and PR branches.

**Plan.** A wiki page, linked from the SDK hub, covering:
- daily drive on stable (or edge, for those who accept breakage)
- keep the VM on edge
- test a PR branch in the VM (check out the branch, run the installer from it, `aphotic doctor`)
- reset the VM after a failed test
- what the required CI checks run, and how to run them locally first with `tools/ci/local.sh`

Every command on the page must exist and match its current flags.

**Done when.** The page exists, is linked from the hub, and every command in it is covered by the drift check ticket.

add.issue.name: Docs stay current: drift checks for the SDK, CLI reference and agent guides

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** SDK pages, the CLI reference and the agent kit guide describe commands and flags that change on dev every week. Prose that nothing checks goes stale. The wiki sync workflow already computes drift between the repo and the wiki, but only for what it knows about.

**Plan.**
- Generate the CLI reference from the `# @cmd` headers the CLI already carries, instead of maintaining it by hand.
- Add a test that extracts every `aphotic …` command, `install.sh` flag and `tools/devvm` subcommand quoted in the SDK pages and the agent kit guide, and fails when one no longer exists.
- Extend the existing wiki drift report to the SDK pages.
- Run on every PR into dev and on the release PR into main, so main's docs match main and dev's match dev.

**Done when.** Renaming a CLI flag without updating the SDK fails CI, and the CLI reference regenerates with no hand edits.

add.issue.comment.md: Scope note (operator, 2026-10-06): the generated guide gets one or two lines pointing at the Developer SDK hub (8D66Q36) for users who run a hypervisor or a dev environment. Nothing more; the SDK is the advanced path and lives on the wiki, so the guide stays short.
